Status: Implemented; independent read-only review completed; synthetic tests passed; no live game or UI actions

Sources.Labels: item_catalog_en.json sourced from local item/msg data; live mod tables may differ

Contract.Descriptor: Engine-owned command table record, never stack temporary; pending operation keeps IDs and actor, not command pointer.
Contract.Restore: No persistent trainer patch. Engine completes/cleans up transition; no automatic revert/reset/second dispatch.
Contract.Ownership: Game thread only; fresh host heartbeat nonzero and <=5000ms; fresh validated player/status/scene; actor replacement owned by engine.
Contract.InputPolicy: Trigger1..5 only, unlocked form and base Sora mode1. Revert form1..6 mode2. Active summons/events/menus/capture/pause/transitions/dead/special/attached actor rejected.
Contract.Outcome: Native Anti/Final random selection preserved; native costs, usage and Final-unlock side effects preserved.

Tests.Scope: Synthetic fake memory and callback counters only, plus embedded original command-byte fixtures for all5 forms/Revert. No process discovery, injection or game native calls. Uses the actual shared ProgressionFeatures.inl read-only rebuild helpers in the fake-memory harness.

Limitations: No live execution test has been performed. The tests validate trainer gates/dispatch exactly once, not native asset loading, animation or post-transition status.
No forced Antiform, no locked-form bypass, no infinite/discount Drive cost. Requested form may yield native Anti/Final result.
Heap allocation and asynchronous asset loading retain native failure assumptions; code validates current structures/model table availability but cannot guarantee future allocations/files.
Guards intentionally reject modified command schemas, patched entry points, unsupported actor variants, form-to-form direct changes and special scenes.
Current player can be replaced on a later native frame. Common bridge must reacquire TrainerContext after each command and ongoing feature leases must follow their existing identity rules.
